end.summary:
Practised representing 11–20 as one bundle of ten and some loose ones.
Saanvi identified 11, 13, 14, and 16 using ten plus loose ones during discussion.
They counted the bundle as one item in several attempts, leading to incorrect totals.
The meaning of the 1 in 15/17 as one ten remained unresolved at the end.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised making numbers 11–20 with one bundle of ten and loose ones. Using “ten and some more” helped them say numbers such as 13, 14, and 16, but they still mixed up the bundle’s ten sticks with counting it as one stick; this was not corrected by the end. At home, build one group of 10 objects and add 1–9 more, then say both the total and “one ten and ___ ones.”
